_note: Fictional families for the resilience engine. Every figure is made up. Amounts are pence. The expected months are worked out by hand from the family's own figures (savings divided by the monthly shortfall, whole months), not copied from the engine, so a mismatch is a finding. apps/api/src/resilience/__tests__/synthetic-families.test.ts checks these against the engine and the profile schema.

families.story: Couple and one child. One main earner, no protection, no life cover.

income_stops.why: 10,000 saved, 2,500 spent a month, no income: 4 months.

families.story: Single adult. Income protection pays 1,000 a month.

income_stops.why: Shortfall is 2,000 spent minus 1,000 protection = 1,000 a month. 6,000 saved: 6 months.

families.story: Couple with life cover of 15,000. The payout arrives 1 to 2 months after a death, so the answer is a range.

earner_dies.why: Late payout (month 2) runs out after 1 month. Early payout (month 1) lasts 6 months.

families.story: Self-employed adult. A business pays 1,500 of the 3,000 monthly income.

income_stops.why: 9,000 saved, 3,000 a month and no income: 3 months.

business_stops.why: Losing 1,500 of income leaves a 1,500 shortfall. 9,000 saved: 6 months.
